items.title: With just one warhead, China sends a reminder of growing military capacity
items.description: This latest military test demonstrates China's growing willingness to use its military strength to send a warning to the Pacific: that Beijing now has the military and nuclear means to assert its dominance in the region.

items.title: Qantas customers warned not to delete email about $105m settlement
items.description: More than 1 million Qantas customers are being notified they may be eligible for access to a multi-million-dollar settlement.

items.title: Officer filmed punching man was using 'approved manoeuvre', police say
items.description: NSW Police say an officer filmed repeatedly punching a man in the back of the head on in Western Sydney on Monday night was using an "approved manoeuvre".

items.title: YouTube doubles down on 'false flag' video about Bondi Beach victim
items.description: YouTube's head of policy tells the Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion a video calling the Bondi Beach terror attack a "false flag" does not breach its hate speech policies.

items.title: Prosecutors argue man accused of killing Charlie Kirk should stand trial
items.description: Utah prosecutors have begun presenting their case against Tyler James Robinson, the man accused of killing conservative activist Charlie Kirk, at a week-long preliminary trial.

items.title: Tributes flow for Nathan Fitzgerald following game day head injury
items.description: The younger brother of footy player and teacher Nathan Fitzgerald, who died last night, has described him as a "gentle, wonderful" soul who cherished his family.

items.title: Jai Arrow marries partner months after MND diagnosis
items.description: The former Rabbitohs and Queensland NRL player has married his partner Berina Colakovic in a small ceremony in Sydney, months after revealing his motor neurone disease diagnosis.

items.title: Accused double killer Beau Lamarre-Condon's mother granted bail
items.description: Coleen Lamarre has been in custody since April, when she was arrested in Sydney's inner west accused of attempting to influence a key witness in her son's upcoming double murder trial.

items.title: 'Not his fault': Belgium coach consoles Balogun after World Cup controversy
items.description: Belgium did not feel it was fair Folarin Balogun played for the US in the round of 16 match after he was given a red card in his team's previous match.

items.title: Execs try to hose down Kayo cost concerns as NRL rights deal revealed
items.description: As the NRL reveals its new broadcast rights deal worth billions of dollars over seven years in 2028 through 2034, executives try to hose down concerns about rising subscription prices.

items.title: Suspected bird flu case detected in SA but yet to be confirmed as H5
items.description: A suspected H5 bird flu case has been detected in a giant petrel on SA's Yorke Peninsula, but the state government says the viral load is low, with further results expected within the next 48 hours.

items.title: 'Shouldn't be living like that': Runner speaks out after being harassed on morning run
items.description: A Brisbane mother says police can improve the way they respond to harassment complaints after she was followed by a car during her morning run.

items.title: Government commits to fix dam that 'cannot be repaired'
items.description: The Queensland government announces a plan to rebuild the Paradise Dam wall where it is, despite its operator previously saying there were too many issues to fix it.

items.title: Blame game rages as hospital emergency department overflows
items.description: Launceston General Hospital's emergency department was overflowing on Monday night, with the nursing union describing the scenes as "chaotic" and "unsafe" — as Tasmania's health minister blames the federal government for a lack of action.

items.title: This Place: Stories of Gurlbin-wula
items.description: This is Gurlbin-wula, part of Man-galagun — where the red dirt meets the turquoise waters on the edge of Broome.  It's a place of spirit birds, storytelling, and deep connection to land. As part of NAIDOC Week the ABC is looking at Indigenous peoples' connection to country, and what makes it so special. NAIDOC Week is marking 50 years of Deadly and runs from July 5 until July 12.

items.title: What you need to know before claiming your phone as a tax deduction
items.description: The cost of buying and using your own phone may be tax deductible, but the ATO has specific rules about how employees calculate these expenses.

items.title: ABC Places quiz: Where in the world are we?
items.description: Your challenge in today's ABC Places quiz is to work out the location of 10 photos from around the world. Be warned: we might try to trick you.

items.title: The 'walking archive' helping First Nations people discover family history
items.description: For 28 years, Ali Abdullah-Highfold has helped thousands of Indigenous people find familial connections through his work at the South Australian Museum.

items.title: Widow not told of husband's death on FIFO swing until 14 hours later
items.description: A Perth widow says she has been kept in the dark about the circumstances leading to the death of her husband as he worked on an offshore gas plant.

items.title: Almost half of Qld prisoners returning to custody within two years, report finds
items.description: The auditor-general has found Queensland Corrective Services (QCS) is not effectively planning or facilitating the rehabilitation and reintegration of its prisoners.

items.title: Regional town's bid to turn showground into world standard Olympic venue
items.description: Toowoomba is the proposed venue for the 2032 Olympic equestrian event, and while excitement is building, questions remain about how they will pull it off.

items.title: SA premier condemns 'fight club' but teens vow to continue bouts
items.description: South Australia's premier says he is appalled by an amateur children's "fight club", while the state's police minister says people who post videos of the fights online may face legal action on top of the participants in the bouts.

items.title: Remote NT MLA admits to claiming travel allowance during stays at city home
items.description: Manuel Brown's dumping from the role comes after weeks of scrutiny over his driving record and confirmation he allowed two of his underage children to drive his personal car on an outstation.

items.title: Boys major victims of AI-assisted online sexual abuse, study finds
items.description: About one in every 25 Australians under the age of 18 has been the victim or knows a victim of artificial intelligence-assisted online sexual abuse, according to a new study.

items.title: Origin legacies and futures on the line for NSW in decider
items.description: As New South Wales look to rise from the ashes and pull off a Lang Park Origin heist, the future of the team and the legacy of some of its greatest players will be tested in the furnace of a decider.
